_about: What one adult needs each day, nutrient by nutrient: the targets the survival garden optimiser
(scripts/survival-garden.js, docs/design/survival-garden.md) holds a garden to. Written 2026-11-06.
Energy and protein are the two tiers of data/closed_loop/person.ron (bare 2,100 kcal and 57 g,
comfort 2,600 kcal and 75 g), so the garden and the closed-loop test size the same person.
Everything else is the US Dietary Reference Intakes for adults aged 19 to 50. The garden must feed
whoever lives in the home, so design_target is the HIGHER of the male and female value, times a
factor where the DRI report itself says a plant-only diet needs more (iron 1.8, zinc up to 1.5).
An RDA covers nearly all healthy people (97 to 98 percent); an AI is set where no RDA could be.
kind: rda, ai, or derived (computed below from a cited pattern). from_plants: how a garden can meet it:
yes        crops carry it and USDA measured it; the optimiser holds the garden to it
medium     crops carry what their soil or nutrient solution gives them (USDA's value is US farm
soil), so the garden is not sized to it: it is reported at USDA's value and closed in
the medium (data/garden/survival_garden.json gaps). Holding it would size the whole
garden to a number the bed, not the crop, decides (the first run did exactly that).
no         no plant makes it (B12, vitamin D); the ship covers it, see data/garden/survival_garden.json gaps
unmeasured USDA SR Legacy does not measure it for these foods; reported, never assumed
ul: the Tolerable Upper Intake Level and what it applies to. Where the DRI says a UL counts only
supplements or fortificants (magnesium, vitamin E, niacin, folate) or only preformed vitamin A,
food from a garden cannot reach it and the optimiser does not hold the garden to it.

person_ron.title: data/closed_loop/person.ron, tiers bare and comfort
person_ron.by: this repository (its own sources quoted on each tier)

reference.ages: 19 to 50 years, male and female, not pregnant or lactating

amino_acids._how: Each indispensable amino acid's target is the FAO adult scoring pattern (mg per g of protein) times the tier's protein target, which is the FAO's own test of a diet: at its safe protein intake the score of every amino acid is at least 1. Counted as eaten: USDA gives total amino acids, not the share the gut absorbs (FAO's DIAAS uses ileal digestibility), so the report prints each amino acid's margin and says whether it would survive a digestibility of 85 percent.

nutrients.label: Iron
nutrients.factor_why: iom_2001_iron: plant iron is absorbed about 10 percent against 18 percent from a mixed diet
nutrients.ul_note: reported, not held: the DRI set it from stomach upsets with iron supplements

nutrients.label: Magnesium
nutrients.ul_note: the UL (350 mg) counts a pharmacological agent only, not food

nutrients.label: Zinc
nutrients.factor_why: iom_2001_zinc: up to 50 percent more for vegetarians, the top of the stated range

nutrients.label: Selenium
nutrients.medium_why: plants do not need selenium and take up what the medium holds; USDA's values are US farm soils

nutrients.label: Sodium
nutrients.no_why: crops carry little; the body's need is met by salt (survival_garden.json gaps)

nutrients.label: Vitamin A
nutrients.ul_note: the UL (3,000 ug) is preformed vitamin A only; plants carry carotenoids

nutrients.label: Vitamin D
nutrients.no_why: no green plant makes it; UV-flashed mushrooms, UV-B on skin, or a supplement (survival_garden.json gaps)

nutrients.label: Vitamin E
nutrients.ul_note: the UL (1,000 mg) counts supplemental alpha-tocopherol only

nutrients.label: Niacin (B3)
nutrients.factor_why: the RDA is niacin equivalents; USDA's niacin is the preformed vitamin only, so the tryptophan the diet also carries (60 mg makes 1 mg) is a margin not counted
nutrients.ul_note: the UL (35 mg) counts supplements and fortificants only

nutrients.label: Folate
nutrients.ul_note: the UL (1,000 ug) counts synthetic folic acid only

nutrients.label: Vitamin B12
nutrients.no_why: only bacteria make it; a supplement or fortified food made by fermentation, or animal food (survival_garden.json gaps)

amdr_pct_energy._note: Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges (dri_2019_tables): the comfort tier holds fat inside its range; the bare tier reports it only, because the range is about long-term disease risk, not survival.
